source.plan: Database query languages: what runs, what to add (owner-approved 2026-09-30, decisions D1-D6)

tierDefinitions.T1: A developer arriving from a competing engine hits it in the first week. Build all of it.
tierDefinitions.T2: Production applications need it. Build selectively, in order.
tierDefinitions.T3: Competitive depth. Deferred; revisit after T2.
tierDefinitions.Fix first: Correctness defect or shared-parser rule that gates every tier.
tierDefinitions.Prerequisite: Not a language family; T1 cannot be exercised without it.
tierDefinitions.Out: Explicitly rejected by a recorded decision.

tierBoardOptionsNote: Keys are the Tier field option names Stage 0 creates; values are the plan tier they mean. A Tier option not listed here is an unknown tier and raises a warning.

T2.note: per-language | global | none. per-language: each T2 family is sequenced after the T2 family the plan lists before it in the same language table. The order positions T2 work; it never blocks it.

T3.note: T3 is deferred and has no stated order: one column.

decisions.ruling: ISO + PostgreSQL spellings (LIMIT, $1, ||, BYTEA, JSONB). Lexical SQL Server aliases only (TOP, NVARCHAR, DATETIME2, IDENTITY(1,1)); no T-SQL procedural language.
Rebase on SQL++, keep the OQL name, drop DEFINE/ELEMENT/FLATTEN, adopt SQL++ MISSING semantics for absent paths.
ISO GQL canonical; accept Cypher spellings that map 1:1 (SKIP, UNWIND as FOR, WITH as RETURN ... NEXT); MERGE is a T2 extension; no FOREACH or procedures.
T1 in full for all three languages, T2 in the order listed, T3 deferred.
Silent-parse defects and the shared parser first; Documents wire server and client (#190) before OQL T1; then SQL, OQL and GQL T1 in parallel.
One feature per language per tier under the existing epics (#4 SQL, #5 Documents, #50 Graph); one task per family; shared-parser work under #31.

T2 "in the order listed" is read per language: SQL 15 steps, OQL 8, GQL 7, Shared 1, not one 31-step list. The order positions T2 work and never blocks it; a family may still be skipped (realignment decision 16, approved 2026-10-16).
#190 (Documents wire server and client) runs BEFORE OQL T1 - not alongside #1126. Every OQL T1 task waits on it.

decisions.topic: Bulk ingest (owner request: bulk upload for every engine)
decisions.ruling: (a) Bulk ingest is engine, wire and client work outside the language tiers. #1656 (under #1519, category L03.02.01.C16: it spans models) is the one contract; each engine path keeps its model's category (C16 boundary): #1545, #1546 and #1547 under #1519, #1657 under #1612, #1658 under #1613, #1659 under #1614. (b) Each batch is its own transaction, committed in order; a failed batch leaves earlier ones committed; a load is refused inside an explicit transaction. PostgreSQL COPY is instead all-or-nothing in the caller's transaction; RavenDB cuts server batches past 16 MiB or at 8,192 operations and awaits each (src/Raven.Server/Documents/Handlers/Processors/BulkInsert/AbstractBulkInsertHandlerProcessor.cs:119-123). (c) bulk is a core capability gating shared frames; capabilities extend 2.1 without a version bump (Database.Protocol/docs/DESIGN.md:267-268). (d) A reject carries the single-record write's error: message, and code where one exists. (e) Only spellings join the plan: sql-copy (T2; server-side files and PROGRAM stay COHDBL001, as PostgreSQL reserves them to the pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files and pg_execute_server_program roles, src/backend/commands/copy.c:82, :93, :102) and gql-load-csv (T3; Cypher with no ISO GQL counterpart, Neo4j community/cypher/front-end/ast/src/main/scala/org/neo4j/cypher/internal/ast/Clause.scala:446, read from a client-sent stream, an exception to D3's 1:1 rule). OQL gets no statement: Couchbase loads with cbimport, and RavenDB bulk-inserts through an endpoint, not RQL (src/Raven.Server/Documents/Handlers/BulkInsert/BulkInsertHandler.cs:10). (f) sql-copy is appended after the SQL table, so #1545 positions no other SQL T2 family; SQL T2 grows from D4a's 15 steps to 16. Placement delegated by the owner.

families.name: COPY ... FROM STDIN / TO STDOUT
families.today: No; COPY is an unknown command (SQL0002)
families.expected: PG COPY FROM STDIN / TO STDOUT; SQL Server BULK INSERT; MySQL LOAD DATA [LOCAL] INFILE
families.add: T2: FROM STDIN and TO STDOUT; server-side files and PROGRAM get COHDBL001 (D7); BULK INSERT and LOAD DATA are not added (D1)
families.notes: Spelling only (D7). FROM STDIN runs on #1545's bulk stream (the filed task depends on #1545), and rows pass INSERT's admission (ExecuteInsertRowsAsync, SqlPlanExecutor.InsertSelect.cs:49), as PostgreSQL COPY FROM runs ExecConstraints per row (copyfrom.c:1360). Batches commit on their own (D7 b), so COPY inside BEGIN gets a coded error, as does COPY without the negotiated bulk capability (#1656). TO STDOUT streams through DatabaseStreamingExchange, as Blob downloads do (BlobConnection.cs:503).

families.name: LOAD CSV [WITH HEADERS] FROM ... AS row
families.today: No; generic COHDBL001 (LOAD is not in the unsupported-word table)
families.expected: Cypher only; no ISO GQL counterpart
families.add: T3, a Cypher extension read from a client-sent stream, not a URL (D7)
families.notes: Spelling only (D7). Cypher's FROM is a URL the server fetches; Neo4j gates file: URLs with two settings (GraphDatabaseSettings.java:427, :437) and http(s): only with an internal IP blocklist (GraphDatabaseInternalSettings.java:82). Both stay COHDBL001: FROM names a client-sent stream (the filed task picks the spelling) whose rows feed #1547's online batches, bound as lists or, WITH HEADERS, maps (#1145, #1146). Client-built batches already work as UNWIND $rows AS row CREATE (#1145, #1146, #1138); this family adds server-side CSV parsing.

items.title: Query-language platform T1: strict parsing, EXPLAIN and coded diagnostics across SQL, OQL and GQL
SQL T1 language surface: the statements, clauses and functions developers expect first
OQL T1 language surface on a SQL++ basis: document DML, DDL, projection, arrays and functions
GQL T1 language surface: ISO/IEC 39075 core with 1:1 Cypher spellings
SQL, OQL, GQL: reject every unsupported keyword and stray character with a coded diagnostic
SQL, OQL, GQL: one parameter contract ($name, @name, $n; bare-name ordinal binding; ? and :name rejected)
SQL, OQL, GQL: deliver every rejection as coded diagnostics; declare only executable functions
SQL, OQL, GQL: EXPLAIN returns the chosen plan as rows in one shared result shape
Database protocol 1.1: negotiate capabilities and structured diagnostics for SQL and GQL; code Key-Value's 1.0 error text
SQL: join INFORMATION_SCHEMA and COHESION_SCHEMA relations like stored tables and capture one catalog snapshot
SQL: execute FETCH FIRST, OFFSET before LIMIT and SELECT TOP
SQL: accept ISO multi-word type names and SQL Server lexical type aliases in DDL and CAST
SQL: execute LEFT, CROSS, comma, USING and N-way joins
SQL: parse and execute DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP/INTERVAL, X'hex' and N'' literals and signed and typed DEFAULT literals
SQL: execute IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM, IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN and [NOT] LIKE ... ESCAPE
SQL: execute ORDER BY ... NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST
SQL: execute correlated subqueries, derived tables, and subqueries in UPDATE/DELETE WHERE
SQL: execute UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT [ALL | DISTINCT] wherever a query is accepted
SQL: execute DISTINCT/ALL aggregates and STRING_AGG / LISTAGG string aggregation
SQL: execute non-recursive WITH common table expressions before SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE
SQL: execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ... RETURNING and expose the affected count on SqlResultSet
SQL: execute INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE upserts with EXCLUDED
SQL: execute CAST across every shared type with a defined conversion
SQL: execute 42 T1 scalar functions with plan-time signature checks, a transaction-start clock and INTERVAL arithmetic
SQL: execute ON DELETE SET NULL / SET DEFAULT / NO ACTION and non-literal column defaults
SQL: execute ALTER TABLE RENAME and ALTER COLUMN SET/DROP DEFAULT and SET/DROP NOT NULL
SQL: execute GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY columns and the SQL Server IDENTITY(seed, increment) alias
SQL: execute CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW and DROP VIEW as read-only, catalog-persisted views
SQL: accept START TRANSACTION, WORK and END spellings on the session transaction commands
OQL: rebase the profile on SQL++ and give absent paths MISSING semantics distinct from NULL
OQL: execute IN lists, BETWEEN, LIKE ... ESCAPE and CASE with SQL++ NULL and MISSING rules
OQL: execute SELECT DISTINCT, SELECT VALUE and object/array constructors with one result shape
OQL: execute LIMIT and OFFSET with literals or parameters and one consistent diagnostic
OQL: execute CREATE COLLECTION and DROP COLLECTION with IF [NOT] EXISTS
OQL: execute INSERT INTO ... (KEY, VALUE) VALUES and INSERT ... SELECT with META() key access
OQL: execute DELETE FROM ... [WHERE] using the existing index seeks
OQL: execute UPDATE ... SET/UNSET partial updates over nested and array-index paths
OQL: execute UPSERT INTO ... (KEY, VALUE) whole-document replacement
OQL: execute composite and UNIQUE indexes with IF [NOT] EXISTS on CREATE and DROP INDEX
OQL: execute UNNEST, ANY/SOME/EVERY ... SATISFIES and IN over array values
OQL: execute 34 SQL++ scalar functions from one function table, with plan-time checks and Int64 COUNT
GQL: execute $name and @name parameters bound from the API and Graph wire parameter maps
GQL: execute ISO label expressions, labeled predicates and every ISO edge direction; reject Cypher --> instead of truncating the query
GQL: execute full WHERE expressions (OR/XOR/NOT, arithmetic, IS NULL, IN, string predicates)
GQL: execute RETURN DISTINCT, RETURN *, computed and aliased expressions, and standalone RETURN
GQL: execute ORDER BY with NULLS FIRST/LAST, OFFSET (SKIP alias) and LIMIT
GQL: execute OPTIONAL MATCH with null extension and multiple MATCH clauses
GQL: execute quantified path patterns ({m,n}, +, *) and Cypher *m..n under trail semantics
GQL: execute linear composition: LET, FILTER, FOR/UNWIND, RETURN ... NEXT and Cypher WITH
GQL: execute CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF and list/map values, including their wire encoding
GQL: execute aggregates (count, sum, avg, min, max, collect_list) with implicit and ISO GROUP BY
GQL: execute a plan-time-checked core function set (element, string, math, CAST, temporal)
GQL: execute SET/REMOVE on properties and labels through an MVCC graph update path
SQL DML parser silently drops trailing tokens: a mistyped WHERE deletes every row
SQL arithmetic faults: division by zero ends the wire session and BIGINT overflow wraps silently
TIMESTAMP and TIMESTAMPTZ index keys disagree with SQL equality
